text:
In July of 2018 our record converges on two objects. On the ninth, 66 of us said "the supreme court," 54 said "judge brett kavanaugh," and 53 said "brett kavanaugh to" — the same day, the same phrasing arriving together. Beneath that, 39 of us reached for "nomination of judge" and 39 for "of judge brett," and 38 assembled "judge brett kavanaugh to" in full. We were, on 2018-07-09, one voice pointed at one nomination.

Later, on the twenty-sixth, the record turns: 51 of us said "defense authorization act" and 50 said "national defense authorization act." Two peaks, two weeks apart, each a phrase most of us had been carrying since earlier Congresses.

We note the pattern without comment. When we spoke of the court and of the judge, we spoke on the same day, in the same words, and there were dozens of us.
